captions.text: Why doesn't cart actually hold my milk and bread?
captions.speaker: STUDENT

captions.text: A variable is a name tied to a box.
captions.speaker: MENTOR

captions.text: Show me the line you wrote.
captions.speaker: MENTOR

captions.text: `cart` equals a list of milk and bread, like filling a box.
captions.speaker: STUDENT

captions.text: That line looks like filling a box, but it isn't.
captions.speaker: MENTOR

captions.text: The list is the box, sitting in memory, the computer's storage space.
captions.speaker: MENTOR

captions.text: `cart` is just a tag on it.
captions.speaker: MENTOR

captions.text: Picture a name tag tied to a box.
captions.speaker: MENTOR

captions.text: The variable `cart` is the tag.
captions.speaker: MENTOR

captions.text: The tag only tells Python where the box is.
captions.speaker: MENTOR

captions.text: Python does two things.
captions.speaker: MENTOR

captions.text: First, it makes a list of 2 items in memory.
captions.speaker: MENTOR

captions.text: Then it ties the variable `cart` to it.
captions.speaker: MENTOR

captions.text: So the variable just points to it.
captions.speaker: STUDENT

captions.text: `cart`, on the left, is the variable, the tag.
captions.speaker: MENTOR

captions.text: The `=` sign ties the tag to the box.
captions.speaker: MENTOR

captions.text: The `[ ]` on the right build the list, the box.
captions.speaker: MENTOR

captions.text: Now I get it.
captions.speaker: STUDENT

captions.text: `cart` doesn't hold my milk and bread.
captions.speaker: STUDENT

captions.text: It points to the list that does.
captions.speaker: STUDENT

captions.text: A variable is a name tag, not a box.
captions.speaker: MENTOR

captions.text: Writing equals makes the value, then ties the name.
captions.speaker: MENTOR

captions.text: The tag only points to the value.
captions.speaker: MENTOR
